To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the design space of interactive public displays is characterized by the three dimensions: (1) the user is in motion, (2) there is a large distance between the user and the display, (3) the user is a casual audience.
public displays can be designed for different interaction modalities and that these modalities can be combined to create exciting and innovative user experiences.
public displays are characterized by their location in public space and that they are designed with a focus on attracting, engaging and motivating users.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of interactive public displays in public space.
the design of interactive public displays.
understanding and designing for the requirements and challenges of interactive public displays.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
interactive public displays should be designed to be attractive, engaging, motivating and fun to use.
the future of public displays will be a combination of the best of all worlds.
the requirements and the design space for interactive multimedia on public screens is very large.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are moving towards the creation of digital environments that allow users to immerse themselves in their favorite content, while moving through urban space.
the design space for interactive multimedia is a complex space, which is characterized by the interplay between the user’s mental models, the interaction modalities and the design of the content.
the design of interactive public display is a complex process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no single design solution for public displays but that the design space has to be carefully considered for every new design and application scenario.
the design space for interactive displays is large and that there is no one size fits all solution.
the user is in control of the experience, the user decides when and where the interaction takes place and how long it lasts.
